summary: Lemma gcd(4Cp+1,4C'p+1) | (C'-C) is one line (C'(4Cp+1)-C(4C'p+1)=C'-C); checked with 0 violations for p up to 2017, C<60, and common divisors never exceed tau(C'-C). Repo's gcd lemma (free_fable sanity script, BRAINSTORM/z52b_free_fable.md) has only the weaker 4(C'-C) form; overlap bound is tiny but does not by itself control the second moment.

F2 relaxation (-1 in span of prime-factor classes mod squares) was tested for all 57,450 (p<6000 with p≡1(4), C≤150) pairs: it is necessary (0 wins without it) but holds in 16,736 pairs of which only 1,522 win (9.1%), so the linear layer is far from sufficient. The genus-layer lemma itself is already in the repo (Z52_BANKED genus layer).

Reproduced exactly: 8229 pairs (p<3000, C<40), 2356 have subgroup∋-1, of which 1695 (=20.6% of pairs) fail. Stratified by omega(N), agreement is far from the claimed >=95% at omega=4 (only 395/4558 = 8.7% of subgroup-containing pairs win); repo already has this as BRAINSTORM/z52b_free_fable.md #201.

Exact C=2 taxonomy checked for p≡1(4), p<6000 (0 mismatches): C=2 wins iff 8p+1 has a sub-product ≡7 mod 8, i.e. fails iff all prime factors of 8p+1 are ≡1,3 (mod 8) or all ≡1,5 (mod 8) (proof: 7 ∉ <1,3> and 7 ∉ <1,5>). This is the C=2 analogue of the repo's C=1 criterion; only C=2 was done here.

Lookup of the stabiliser test on all ω(N)≥6 C-form failures (p≡1(4)≤1e5, C≤200): 1329 failures, of which 1279 have trivial stabiliser (aperiodic) and only 50 are periodic; the 'rich failures are periodic' dichotomy is refuted.

Reproduced: among Omega>=5 failures (p<6000, C<150) 2531 of 4184 (60.5%) have subgroup∋-1 (multiplicity-poverty), the other ~39.5% are Galois-type; matches the repo's 61/39 split (free_fable summary item 4). The threshold |D|≥phi(4C) regime is tiny (784 failures), with 172 of them multiplicity-type.

Max denominator/p² over all solutions (dumps, p≡1(4)≤2e4) is unbounded in practice (max ≈4.2e6 at p=19997): solutions with huge z exist, so the extremal quantity is the minimum (minz), not the max; the Curtiss-type bound does not apply to this quantity.

Literature check: sets avoiding 1/x+1/y=1/z (Ruzsa/Erdős-type results, found via web search) concern the homogeneous reciprocal equation; ES is inhomogeneous 4/n, so no density bound transfers without a new argument.
evidence: web search: 'sets without solutions to 1/x+1/y=1/z density Ruzsa Erdos'

summary: Level graph (C≤400, edges = shared prime q≤200): hard primes 409, 577, 5569, 9601 and controls 401, 433, 1009, 2521 all show ~80 isolated C, giant fraction 0.78–0.80, and no difference in components or λ2 (λ2 is 0 only when disconnected).

Precise version: approximate counts with residue tolerance k around -1 mod 4C are a restatement of equidistribution of divisor residues; the exact count is the δ=0 slice and no separate test was found to differ.
'Share a winning C' graph on 600 primes ≡1(4): degree median 469 of 599 (density 0.72), so the graph is dense; the local-limit object is trivial (no sparse neighbourhood structure).

Computable part: work to the first certificate (least winning C) over p≤1e6 has records 39 (p=4789), 141 (19141), 251 (60217), 557 (98017); only 14 primes ≤1e6 have no winner ≤1000. Heuristically easy to search, which is the observation the item wanted; no hardness assumption is derived from it.
Host-graph version: if certificates are the edges of a host graph H_p, supersaturation counts edges themselves; no host with edges ≠ certificates was defined, so the pattern-counting step is vacuous.
Same as Z1892: a 2-path count in a graph whose edges are the certificates is the certificate count itself; no separate graph was identified to test Blakley–Roy.

Matroid of 2-adic character vectors of prime factors = the F2 'genus' relaxation of Z1478; its rank/deficiency statistics are those computed there (relaxation necessary, win rate 9.1% among relax-holding pairs).

Solution graph for p≤2e4 (edge = shared denominator): median 5 components (max 13); edges sharing two denominators never occur (the third is determined), so 'moves' are single-denominator only and the graph is fragmented.

Lookup: 'A proof of the Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture' (arXiv 2101.04698, Kang–Kelly–Kühn–Methuku–Osthus) confirmed; absorption needs a rich approximate structure plus an absorber set, and no ES analogue of either was identified.
Erdős's 1950 covering for p+2^k (Summa Brasil. Math. 2) confirmed by web search; it is a covering of the complement of a different sumset, and ES has no analogous finite covering (B1 in the repo).
Absorption analogy only: no leave set or absorber for the ES certificate families is defined, and the graceful-tree literature gives no transferable step.

The critical group of any multigraph with τ=p prime is Z/p (order p is prime), so the sandpile state invariant for ES words is only p and its pairing class (Z2651); no further conserved quantity exists to compare.
Wang-tile local-to-global analogy: the item itself says no finite-state reduction exists for ES; no local tile set was constructed, so nothing is tested.
Sumset test in F_p: A={1/a : a≤N}; |A+A|/|A| = 12.5 (N=30, p=1009), 14.5 (N=60), 14.0 and 22.0 at p=2521: no small doubling, so no incidence-bound leverage at these scales.
Reciprocal residue sumset (same computation as Z2308): |A+A| ≈ 0.4|A|² with no additive structure visible for N≤60 at p=1009, 2521.
ES equation 4xyz=p(xy+yz+zx) is linear in each variable (no Vieta involution); empirically two distinct solutions never share two denominators, so no Vieta-type move exists at all.

The isolated-prime set of the level-C bipartite graph is the C-form exception set (409, 577, 5569, 9601, ...) already tabulated in the repo (free_fable summary item 1); the graph language adds no new test. Our C≤2000 forensic confirms 409 has no C-form witness.

Lookup: Helfgott–Radziwiłł 'Expansion, divisibility and parity' (arXiv 2103.06853) confirmed; its graphs have edges n~m by divisibility with parity, while the level graph (Z1729) has no expansion (isolated C ≈ 80, giant ≈ 0.8 for hard and easy primes alike).
Lookup: Hanson–Petridis (arXiv 1905.09134) bounds additive sumsets A+B contained in roots of unity; the repo's χ-product cliques are multiplicative, so the hypothesis does not match the object.
Nullstellensatz gives a grid point where the polynomial is nonzero, i.e. a non-solution; Chevalley–Warning does not apply (degree 3 in 3 variables), so the tool points the wrong way for ES zeros.
No hypergraph of failure sets is defined; container bounds need bounded codegrees, which is not checkable for the ES families; no computation possible from the item as stated.
Lookup: Moreira 'Monochromatic sums and products in N' (arXiv 1605.01469) is a colouring theorem; ES failure is not a colouring of N, so the transfer does not apply.
Lookup: Mattheus–Verstraëte 'The asymptotics of r(4,t)' (arXiv 2306.04007) constructs algebraic graphs; the repo's sterile residue sets are not shown to be such graphs, so no test was possible.
Lookup: Marcus–Spielman–Srivastava interlacing families (arXiv 1304.4132) need a real-rooted family; ES certificates give no real-rooted polynomial family, so the mechanism is not available.

Lookup: the 'weighted dilation graphs' preprint is an unrefereed GitHub PDF (openai/math) cited by arXiv 2610.15674; its object is p−1 smoothness, which correlates with U/log²p only weakly (Spearman 0.20, Z0812), not N_e smoothness.
Lookup: Dias da Silva–Hamidoune (Bull. LMS 26, 1994) concerns restricted sums in Z/p; ES product sets live in (Z/4C)^× which is not cyclic of prime order, so the bound does not apply.
evidence: web search: Dias da Silva Hamidoune 1994

summary: Log-concavity of a_k = #{(p,C): C wins, ω(C)=k} over p≡1(4)≤1e5: a = [3556, 13695, 8957, 1135], log-concave at both interior points; the sequence has four terms, so this is weak evidence only.
Lookup: Adiprasito–Huh–Katz (arXiv 1511.02888) gives Hodge-theoretic positivity for matroids; no ES count was identified as a matroid invariant (the item itself expects none).

Hashimoto (non-backtracking) spectral radius of the C–q bipartite graph (C≤300) is 6.296 at p=409 and 6.296 at control p=401 (degree-irregular, so the Ramanujan comparison is only indicative); no hard-prime signal.
gcd(tn+1, t'n+1) divides t'-t by the same identity as Z1477, so the GCD-graph overlap is determined by t-t' alone; nothing beyond the coupling lemma.
Restatement of ES₅: det M = tuv−u−v = p and (M⁻¹)₁₁ = (tu−1)/p (checked by hand), so the non-square pairing is the Legendre class of tu−1; enumerating fans only relists ES₅ words.

Triangle multigraphs (τ = xy+yz+zx = p, pairing class ((x+y)/p), so k*=3 when non-square) exist for all 1125 primes p≡1(4), p≤2e4; the criterion holds at 43 primes where the C≤5 certificate does not, so it is a different witness family. It is not shown to imply ES.
next: Decide whether a non-square triangle (x,y,z) yields an explicit ES decomposition of 4/p (try the map from the triangle to 3-term denominators), and test whether the 43 extra primes are the ones with C-form failures at C≤200.

summary: Lookup: arXiv 2503.23648 ('The spanning tree spectrum') proves that every residue u mod N is τ(G) mod N for a planar G on O(log N) vertices; it controls τ mod N, not the sandpile pairing class, so no ES-sign control follows.
Idoneal test (h(−4n) = #genera) on the U-sporadics: only 105 is idoneal (8 = 8); 2961 (48 vs 8), 3985 (24 vs 4), 25305 (80 vs 16), 111969 (240 vs 16), 978145 (424 vs 8) are not.

Sylver-coinage Grundy values (names ≤24, 22 forest-edge pairs with uv|p+u+v at p∈{73,97,401,409,577,1009,2521}): QR edges take values {1,4,5,8}, QNR edges {2,3,4,6,8,9,10}, overlapping; no separation at this truncation.

Lookup: Brooks–Smith–Stone–Tutte squared rectangles (web search: 'Brooks, Smith, Stone, Tutte Parts I/II' and 'Determinants and current flows') confirm the electrical-network correspondence; no map from the fan to a tile-parity observable is given in them, so the test was not defined.

Strip/domino involution: no weighted tiling model for tu−1 or tuv−u−v is given in the item, and the tiling count reduces to continuant recurrences already in the repo; no sign-reversing involution is produced.
Hermitian ℤ/4 connection Laplacian of the fan with random unit holonomies on each edge: det = p in 200/200 cases, so the connection is gauge-trivial on this graph and carries no ES sign information.
Forests are bipartite, so the spectrum of F_p is symmetric (λmin = −λmax) and the Hoffman bound gives α/V = 0.5 exactly for all tested p≤1200: the bound is vacuous.
Component/QNR question on the forest F_p is the existing FOREST_CONNECTIVITY.md analysis (monochromatic component of 1 at p=409 with negative word (15,4,7) already recorded).

F₂ flat-colouring space (constancy on forest edges + multiplicativity for k=2,3,5) has dimension ≥3 for 178 of 180 primes, and the Legendre colouring is never in it (every p has a bichromatic forest edge); the constraints do not force a global obstruction.
CHJ frieze-with-coefficients ↔ ES₅ words is already in FRIEZE_ES.md (30 keyword hits).
Mod-4 frieze/quiddity reduction is covered by FRIEZE_ES.md and the slot lemma already in the repo; no new counting done.
Restatement: by the slot lemma (FOREST_CONNECTIVITY.md Thm 2.1) 'some pentagon entry ≡0 mod 4' is exactly the ES₅ sign condition, so the tropical 2-adic pattern question is ES itself.
Laurent/cluster description of the pentagon with coefficient and the divisor condition (cm-1)|(N+c) is already in FRIEZE_ES.md and BRAINSTORM/y2_zamolodchikov_forcing.md.
SL2-tiling / Farey path reading with mod-4 holonomy is already analysed in the repo around arXiv:2312.12953 (BRAINSTORM/y2_farey_complex_lifting.md, FRIEZE_ES.md).

Lookup: Fock–Goncharov 'Cluster ensembles, quantization and the dilogarithm' (2009) gives A/X duality; no dual variety for the coefficient pentagon is identified in the item, and no tropical integer-point count was computable.

Lookup: Caldero–Chapoton and Cuntz–Holm–Jørgensen (arXiv 1909.02332, title verified) categorify friezes; the Frobenius category for coefficient friezes is not identified in the literature found, so no Euler-characteristic test exists.
lambda(p) (continued-fraction length, <=3 for ES) and the S_L(p) ladder are in the repo (CONTEXT lists lambda(p)<=3; ZAREMBA_TRANSFER.md tracks the L-ladder).
Percolation/giant-component reading of F_p is the FOREST_CONNECTIVITY.md question; the QNR-in-component-of-1 criterion is already recorded there.

Erdős–Selfridge potential needs a hypergraph of residue-class edges; the natural version (edges = residue classes mod 4C where C wins) is determined by the class-wide certification data already tabulated (Z3018), which leaves 22 classes uncovered at C≤50.

SIGN_IDENTITY.md (O205) gives no positive identity for N-; it has only size/modular-form obstructions (PROVED Thm 2.2, Prop 2.3), so there is no signed identity whose terms could be given involutions. Not pursued further.
Pfaffian/Kasteleyn identity needs a planar graph whose perfect matchings are certificates; no such graph is defined, and the Kasteleyn reference (1961) gives no ES-specific object.
The 1-D Sperner/bichromatic-edge argument behind H4 is FOREST_H4.md; a 2-D labelling is not specified by the item.
Lorenzini critical polynomial / Wang–Lu density-1 and the A3 sandpile reading of I3 are the content of LORENZINI_W.md (21 keyword hits).

Analytic: T(-1,-1) of any graph is ±2^(bicycle dim) (Rosenstiehl–Read), so the (-1,-1) evaluation of the fan carries only power-of-2 data, no Legendre information; T(1,1)=p is the only p-sensitive evaluation. The other roots-of-unity evaluations were not computed.

Dilogarithm five-term relation needs the pentagon X-coordinates as rationals; the item gives no closed form, and torsion claims for Bloch group elements would require a separate computation not supported here.
Subgroup generated by all forest edge products uv (edges of F_p) equals F_p^* for 180 of 180 primes p≡1(4), p≤2500, so the sufficient condition 'edge products generate' holds throughout this range.
Brown–Rödl partition regularity of 1/x+1/y=1/z is already cited in the repo (BRAINSTORM/z52b_analogues.md, z52b_free_opus.md) and the transport-law framing is in TRANSPORT_LAW.md; no new test.
Duplicate of Z1477 (gcd(4Cp+1,4C'p+1) | C'-C); see Z1477 outcome.

Configuration-model giant (Newman–Strogatz–Watts from the degree sequence of F_p) predicts median giant fraction 0.042, observed largest component median 0.065 over 60 primes p<2500: the forest is close to its degree-sequence null model.

Temperley/dimer reading of the fan requires a height-function sign that is not defined in the item; the fan is planar (so a Kasteleyn matrix exists) but no observable is specified to compare with the slot-lemma sign.

Positive friezes with boundary (1,1,1,1,N) correspond to positive words tuv−u−v=N, so F(N)=W(N); computed W(n) for n≤800 with records (1,3),(3,6),(5,9),(7,11),(11,15),(17,17),(35,24),(47,31),(119,47).

Move graph on solutions (share one denominator) is fragmented (median 5 components per p≤2e4) and no two solutions share two denominators, so 'moves' cannot connect solutions beyond single denominators; component congruences are then trivial.

Lookup: Croot–Lev–Pach (arXiv 1605.01506, title verified) bounds progression-free sets in Z_4^n; the ES avoidance set is not a subset of an elementary abelian group with a defined linear pattern, so slice rank does not apply directly.
Same obstruction as Z2434: CN yields non-vanishing points; the trial-form shadow is not specified, so no coefficient can be computed.
Reiher-type table for N=4Cp+1 with ω(N)≥4 (p<6000, C≤60): divisors ≡−1 (mod 4C) by number of prime factors: parity counts 550 (even k) vs 458 (odd k), no parity identity visible.
Extremality score E(p)=#{ℓ≤100: (ℓ/p)=1} vs U/log²p over p≡1(4)≤1e5: Spearman −0.14, a weak effect, so the extremal/random split has no strong handle in this data.

Class-wide certification mod 840: a class is certified if some C≤50 wins for every sampled prime in it; 74 classes (covering 77.6% of primes ≡1(4), ≤1e5) are certified and the 22 uncertified classes include all six Mordell hard classes (1,121,169,289,361,529) plus 409, 577, 541, 757 etc. So the discharging-type 'configurations' are the classes of small-prime congruences.
next: Check for each of the 16 non-Mordell uncertified classes whether a prime in it is certified at C≤200 or only at larger C (the R-zeros), and whether the 22-class set equals the set of classes where all primes lack a {3,5,7}-supported certificate.

summary: Pigeonhole over near-certificates needs a defined defect space and combination law; the item leaves both open, and the nearest computable object (the 22 uncertified mod-840 classes, Z3018) gives no collision count.
Certificate-free residues mod q: for q∈{7,11,13,31,101,199} every residue class contains some prime with a C≤20 win (no certificate-free residue), so the Dvir-type set is empty at this resolution.
Zero-sum combination across levels needs a common group for defects; the defect group (ℤ/4C)^× changes with C, and no combination law was produced by the item, so no test is defined.

Erdős–Selfridge consecutive-level mechanism needs explicit thin sets S_C; the explicit C-form sets are the divisor-class sets already tabulated, and the distinctness argument has no computable instance beyond the Z1477 gcd lemma.
Reingold-type amplification (Reingold 2008, log-space connectivity) needs a graph whose connectivity equals ES(p); the level graph (Z1729) is not such a graph (no hard/easy separation).

Min Omega(d) over all C-form certificates (C≤150, p≡1(4), p<6000): 373 primes have a prime witness (Omega=1), 7 have min Omega=2, none needs 3; the only primes with no witness are the known 409, 577, 5569. Empirical 'bounded Omega' holds in range but witnesses are mostly prime, so this is the divisor lottery restated.
A product of coprime divisors is a divisor of the product, so the recursive split re-describes the subset-product set; no new certificates arise.
Surgery moves between levels reduce to the shared-prime graph of Z1729, which shows no separation between hard and easy primes.
Collision test: among ES solutions at fixed p, the share of solutions whose product x·y equals another solution's product is 0.000 for both 100 hard and 100 easy primes (≤2e4).

Minmax-z solution (smallest largest denominator) is Type II (p | y and p | z) for all 1125 primes p≡1(4) ≤2e4, and x | z in only 15 cases; this is the minz ≡ 0 (mod p) fact of fingerprint-0190 (BRAINSTORM/z52b_fingerprint.md).

f(B) = fraction of primes p≡1(4), p≤1e5 with no C-form win for C≤B: 0.2565 (B=1), 0.0983 (2), 0.0179 (8), 0.0090 (16), 0.0042 (32), 0.0023 (100); log f ≈ −0.74 log B, floored at the 8 never-winning primes (0.0017).

AGP-style avoiders: the C≤200 avoidance set at p≡1 mod 24, p≤1e5 is exactly the 8 never-winning primes (409, 577, 5569, 9601, 23929, 60217, 83449, 98017), so there is no room for many simultaneous CRT-dodgers at this scale.
Two-squares candidates x ∈ {a, b, a±b, ab, a²−b², 2a, 2b}·k (k≤4): some candidate gives a two-term 4/p−1/x for only 8 of 267 primes p≡1 (24), p≤2e4 (3%).

Greedy cover of primes p≡1(24), p≤1e5 by C-form sets (C≤200): 23 sets cover all coverable primes; cover size 2, 7, 15, 23 at X=1e3, 1e4, 3e4, 1e5, growing faster than log X (superlog growth) but far below log²X.
Monte-Carlo-style avoidance density replaced by the exact prime-sample version: f(B) (Z0358) — no residue-class sampler needed; decays as B^{-0.74} down to the 8 never-winners.
Character-model R²: log(U/log²p) on (q/p), q≤100, for p≡1(4)≤1e5 gives 5-fold CV R² = 0.094; the class-mod-840 means give CV R² = 0.62. Local class data explain far more than quadratic characters.
OEIS anchors A292581/A292624/A192789 are recorded in the repo (A292624 and A192789 appear in repo memos); b-file extension not re-checked.
minz(n)=A337432 match and records are in the repo's fingerprint memos (A337432 appears in repo).

Proved lemma: if 4∤n, every solution's lcm is divisible by n (odd q|n by valuation; for v2(n)=1, a solution with all-odd denominators would give an odd sum of an even number, contradiction). Converse (4|n gives exceptions) is only the minlcm data, not checked here. Lemma is trivial for ES.
minlcm(p)/p vs least QNR correlation (+0.23) and its practical-number question are fingerprint-0033 in BRAINSTORM/z52b_fingerprint.md.
Record positions of U(n) (n≤3e4) are 2,3,6,8,10,12,15,24,30,40,48,60,…; 20 of 53 U-records are highly-composite (τ) records, so U is not governed by τ-records alone.
All 25 listed record primes > 2 are ≡ 3 (mod 4) (including 18719 ≡ 3), and p ≡ 3 (mod 4) is trivial: 4/p = 1/((p+1)/4) + 1/(p(p+1)/4). The mod-840 pattern is the p≡3 (mod 4) case, not a new effect.
Meta/outreach: OEIS submission is a human publication action, not a mathematical step.
Reproduced R(3^k) for k=1..9 (C≤300): 0,0,2,0,2,0,4,0,18 — T1 kills even k (squares) and the odd values match the item; this is the T1 fingerprint (T1_TEMPLATE.md).

Reproduced the U-certificate zero set (fingerprint-0178 definition, v∈4Z∪(8Z−n), v<1500): zeros include 12, 28, 60, 96, 105, 124, 156, 204, 228, 288, 2961; among n≡1(4) the zeros are odd squares plus 105 (2961 is also a zero), so restricting to n≡1 mod 4 keeps the sporadic zeros.
Safe primes ≤1e5: mean U/log²p = 2.72 vs 2.10 for all p≡3(4); Spearman with log P⁺(p−1)/log p is 0.20. Safe primes are easier, consistent with the item's prediction, but the effect is modest.
Solutions-per-x Gini over p≡1(4)≤2e4: median 0.43 (10–90%: 0.33–0.56); U/nx median 2.13 over primes ≤1e5.

Distinct (x,y,z) residue patterns mod 105 per prime: hard-200 primes have median 38.5 of 39 solutions (almost injective); easy-200 median 103 of 114. Local residue fingerprints barely collapse, so they carry little hardness information.
log U(pq) ~ 4.72 + 0.21 log U(p) + 0.31 log U(q) over composites pq≤3e4 (4441 pairs, R²=0.30): the count is sub-multiplicative (slopes sum to 0.52), not a product of prime counts.

Binary digits: Spearman(hamming weight, U/log²p) = 0.24 over p≡1(24), but hamming weight correlates with log p (ρ=0.38) and U/log²p itself correlates with p (ρ=0.33); the signal is a size trend, not a digit effect.
k-means on the 200 hardest primes (≤1e5) with Legendre/divisibility features: inertia ratio 0.94 (k=2), 0.89 (k=3), 0.86 (k=4); no well-separated clusters.

Isosceles law checked by brute force for p<3000 (no exceptions: 2/a+1/b=4/p and 1/a+2/b=4/p solvable iff p≡3 mod 4); PROVED in fingerprint-0229 (BRAINSTORM/z52b_fingerprint.md) via (4x-2p)(4z-p)=2p². Re-derived independently here.
x|z ⟺ y|z is the one-line identity 4z/p = z/x + z/y + 1 (p|z), already proved in fingerprint-0190 (BRAINSTORM/z52b_fingerprint.md).
Chain x|y|z failure set (670 primes ≤1e5) is in data/z52b/variants2.json; the density question is the only open part.
Prime-x and square-denominator failure sets are in data/z52b/variants.json and variants2.json.
Only-z-divisible-by-n failures at powers of 2 are recorded in data/z52b/variants2.json.

Targeted search: a character model fit on p≤1e5 ranks the 350 primes ≡1 (840) in (1e5,1e6] with correlation 0.38 to the exact log(U/log²p); the predicted-most-solutions top-10 average −0.225 vs −0.535 for the predicted-fewest bottom-10; min U = 46 at p=132721.

Wilson quotient W_p = ((p−1)!+1)/p mod p, normalised to [0,1): Spearman with log(U/log²p) over p≡1(4)≤2e4 is −0.03 (p=0.27), null as expected (an unnormalised version gave a spurious 0.16 from size scaling).

Ramanujan-sum expansion of U(n)/log³n over n≤3e4 (q≤30): R²=0.73; coefficients a1=4.09, a2=2.14, a3=1.47, a4=1.51, a6=0.72 vs a2·a3=3.15 — the coefficients are not multiplicative, so no Euler-product reading.
A392469 record structure is reproduced in repo (data/z52b/raw/mink_pr_2e5.txt, scripts/z52b_fingerprint_mink.c); the restriction p≡1 mod 24 is already noted.
k(p) = min{denominator/p : p | denominator} for p≡1(4), 5≤p≤2e4: records 5,13,37,421,541,1381,3361,16381 with k = 1,2,4,6,10,21,25,32; max k/log p = 3.30 (p=16381), far below the 71 log p bound.

A257843 membership (lex-first solution ≠ max-z solution) reproduces the OEIS terms 89,113,161,…,593 (n≤3000). For primes p≡1(4), p≤2e4 it occurs for 23% of primes, but for 0 of the primes p≡5 (mod 8) (classes 5 and 13 mod 24, ~570 primes), 25% for p≡1 mod 24 and 67% for p≡17 mod 24: membership is confined to p≡1 (mod 8).
next: Prove that for p≡5 (mod 8) the lexicographically first solution has the largest denominator z (a 2-adic argument on the first denominator), and check whether the p≡1 (8) membership rate is governed by p mod 16 or 32.

summary: Lowest U/log³n composites ≤3e4 are odd prime squares (9409=97², 12769=113², 26569=163², 11881=109², 1369=37²), T1-type; only 2 of the 15 lowest have both prime factors ≡1 mod 24.
log U(n) ~ 4.91 + 1.11·ω₁(n) + 1.15·ω₃(n) over 26,754 composites ≤3e4: ω₃ boosts the bulk count as much as ω₁.
Solutions for p≡1(4)≤2e4 (83,652 total): the most common integer ratios are y/x = z/y = 2 (569 each), then 6 and 5; log(y/x) histogram has no sharp peaks beyond these integer ratios.

Lag-840k correlations of log(U/log²p): raw 0.69–0.73; after removing mod-840 class means (cross-fitted) 0.11, 0.26, 0.00, 0.13 for k=1,2,5,10; the residual is correlated at lags preserving p mod 16 (k=2,10) and not at k=1,5, consistent with a 2-adic (mod-16) effect beyond mod 840 (fingerprint-0111).
Size-normalised correlations over p≡1(4)≤7500: Spearman(U/log²p at p, at 4p+1) = 0.21; with (p+3)/4: 0.68 (shared 2-adic data).
